title: The Red Skelton Show
paragraphs: Comedy-variety star vehicle built around Red Skelton recurring characters, sketches and music.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Raleigh Cigarette Program / NBC (October 7, 1941 to June 6, 1944) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Military-service hiatus (June 7, 1944 to December 3, 1945), Post-service NBC return (December 4, 1945 to 1949-04) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and CBS-era Red Skelton Show (1949-04 to 1953-05) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Red Skelton (performer and host), David Rose and His Orchestra (performer), Rod O'Connor (performer and announcer), [[person|lurene-tuttle|Lurene Tuttle]] (performer), Pat McGeehan (performer), Dick Ryan (performer), and The Four Knights (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]].
The stories often return to family and domestic comedy, music and performance, travel and transportation, radio and broadcasting, shopping and consumer life, and jobs and workplace comedy.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes World War II and entertainer military service, Sponsor-driven network comedy, and Radio-to-television transition.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], [[show|let-george-do-it|Let George Do It]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], and [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]].
